title: Offline-first network & upgrade acceptance criteria for private/VPC deployments
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Customers running Redwood Private in isolated VPCs or air-gapped data centers require a deterministic, well-tested upgrade and networking acceptance surface that guarantees zero- or low-egress operation, safe image delivery, and automated rollback without relying on outbound internet access. This ticket defines the PRD-level requirements and specific acceptance criteria for an "offline-first" upgrade and networking model, plus operational playbooks and verification steps for customer success and SRE teams.
background: We've observed multiple private deployment incidents where upgrades failed because control-plane components expected outbound access for image pulls, time sync, or signature validation. Customers ask for explicit guarantees: upgrades must be possible when outbound egress is blocked or when artifacts are mirrored to a customer-hosted registry. This PRD captures requirements for connectivity patterns, artifact staging, validation signals, and verification checks to certify a Private deployment for air-gapped upgrades.
goals: 1) Define minimal network surface required for offline upgrades and normal operation. 2) Specify artifact staging and image signing validation flow that works with local registry mirrors. 3) Produce an upgrade playbook for canary and full rollouts that does not require internet egress. 4) Define acceptance tests and observability checks that indicate a successful offline upgrade.
non_goals: 1) Implementing the orchestration automation (this ticket defines acceptance criteria and playbook only). 2) Supporting arbitrary non-container runtime formats — only OCI/mirrored images and tarball artifacts are in scope. 3) Building a managed mirror service — customers are expected to mirror artifacts to a reachable registry or provide pre-staged artifacts.
scope: Included: network rules and minimal DNS needs, pre-staged artifact validation, image signature verification using customer KMS/HSM or offline key material, canary upgrade steps for Private clusters, verification checks (health, KV cache sanity, model artifact integrity), rollback criteria, and runbook for SRE/SE. Excluded: rewriting of customer's firewall policies and on-site execution of upgrades.
networking_requirements:
- Private control plane must operate without outbound internet if customer provides: (a) mirrored OCI registry reachable from cluster, (b) CRL/OCSP cache or offline trust bundle, and (c) NTP service or time-sync hipri.
- Minimum ephemeral egress allowed: none. If egress is permitted, it must be configurable and scoped to specific hosts.
- DNS: support split-horizon and configurable host overrides; support explicit /etc/hosts or in-cluster DNS entries for artifact endpoints.
- TLS: accept customer-supplied certs and CA bundle for both internal and artifact endpoints.
- Registry auth: support basic auth, token auth, and registry mirror with pre-provisioned credentials stored in KMS or secrets store.
- Health checks: control-plane components must have explicit health endpoints that work over VPC-internal networking.
- Time sync: support internal NTP and tolerance window documented in playbook.
artifact_and_signature_requirements:
- All images/artifacts must be pre-pulled to a customer-accessible registry or provided as image tarballs.
- Image signing: support sigstore/notation or other vendor-neutral signature formats; allow offline signature verification using an uploaded trust root.
- If CRLs/OCSP are unavailable, support a signed trust bundle distributed during staging.
- Customers must be able to supply a signed manifest describing component versions; the installer validates manifest signatures against the trust root before proceeding.
upgrade_playbook_steps: 1) Pre-check: cluster snapshot, resource health, SLO baseline collection (token-level cost/latency sample).
2) Stage artifacts: mirror images to customer registry or upload tarballs to staging buckets accessible within VPC.
3) Validate: run offline signature verification and manifest consistency checks locally; report any mismatches and abort on failure.
4) Canary: deploy new control-plane image to 1-2 nodes running with restricted traffic routing; run smoke tests and KV cache integrity checks for 30 minutes.
5) Observe: verify metrics (latency, error rate, token throughput), run model infer sanity tests against pinned prompts, and confirm logs show no new deserialization or kernel errors.
6) Roll-forward: if canary passes, proceed to staged rollout with configurable batch size (default 25% of nodes).
7) Fallback: if any health check fails or custom QE checks trip, perform automatic rollback using pre-staged prior images and restore pre-upgrade snapshot.
8) Post-upgrade verification: validate all services, run audit log integrity check, attest artifact signatures, and publish upgrade result artifact to local registry.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Upgrade can be completed in an environment with zero outbound internet, given mirrored artifacts and provided trust bundle.
A2: Image signature verification succeeds using uploaded trust root without reaching external CA or OCSP endpoints.
A3: Canary verification includes automated KV-cache integrity checks and regression detection using a small prompt set; regressions block rollout.
A4: Rollback completes within a defined window (target: 10 minutes to restore prior control-plane image and config) and cluster returns to pre-upgrade health baseline.
A5: All network dependencies are documented by hostname/IP and port, and playbook provides mapping to allow firewall rule creation on customer's side.
A6: Upgrade runs produce deterministic audit logs and a signed upgrade result artifact stored in the customer's registry or artifact store.
A7: SRE/SE runbook includes explicit troubleshooting steps for common failures (image pull auth, time skew, DNS misconfiguration) and owner escalation contacts.
test_cases: TC1: Offline upgrade with mirrored registry only - run through playbook in lab VPC with egress blocked and validate A1-A6.
TC2: Manifest tampering - alter manifest signature; verification must fail and upgrade aborts.
TC3: Canary failure simulation - introduce a model artifact mismatch; system should detect regression and trigger rollback automatically.
TC4: Registry auth rotation - change registry credentials mid-stage and verify playbook guidance for secret rotation without downtime.
TC5: Time skew - simulate NTP drift beyond tolerance and validate playbook remediation and abort criteria.

monitoring_and_observability:
- Ensure token-level latency and per-node error rate dashboards exist for the private deployment.
- Add upgrade-specific traces and events to the control-plane timeline.
- Define burn-rate alerts for increased error or token cost post-upgrade with auto-pause option for rollouts.
rollout_criteria_and_limits:
- Default max concurrent upgrade batch: 25% nodes.
- Max allowed errors during rollout: 0.5% of requests OR a sustained 5x increase in 5m error rate compared to baseline—whichever occurs first.
- Canary must run minimum 30 minutes and meet synthetic correctness tests before roll-forward.
notes_and_next_steps:
- Align SRE and Solutions Engineering on lab validation schedule.
- Build verification harness in infra/private-upgrades repo and add a CI job that can run offline-simulated upgrades.
- Schedule security review for signature formats and KMS integration prior to implementation.
review_feedback: 2025-02-14: Security requested explicit mention of key rotation and offline revocation process. Ops requested addition of a pre-flight NTP/time-warp check. Both items added to playbook and tests.
